summary: SSE connection-id rotation truncates in-flight chat generation for long responses
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports consistent truncation of long streaming chat responses when generation passes ~45s. The SSE stream is terminated with no final chunk and no explicit 5xx. Impact: Several long-chat API calls from the customer's dedicated pool are cutting off mid-generation, causing content loss and user-visible partial paragraphs. Environment: Customer in dedicated tier on us-east-1, using SSE chat endpoint. Steps to reproduce:
1) Use SSE chat to request long-form generation (~1k+ tokens) against redwood-v1-13b pinned in customer's dedicated pool.
2) Observe streaming output up to ~45s then abrupt stop without final event.
3) Retry same prompt often succeeds if routed to a different worker without conn-id change.
Logs: initial events show normal token emission, then connection-id rotation event in edge-proxy logs followed by TCP FIN without worker error. No model OOM recorded.
User impact: content truncation in production UI for PaperTrail Labs customers; repeatable across multiple accounts behind the same LB configuration.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Customer (support@papertrail.example): We're seeing partial outputs on long AI summaries. Always around 40-50s into generation the chat stops and the UI shows 'Disconnected'. No error returned from API. Happening ~7/10 requests.
2026-03-10 09:30 - Maya Patel (Support): Acknowledged and escalated to SRE. Requesting logs (X-Request-ID) and approximate timestamps. Opening internal incident INC-20260310-07.

2026-03-10 10:02 - SRE (Anita Gomez): Edge-proxy logs show conn-id reassignment events from the load-balancer cluster at the same timestamps as the truncations. Worker traces show in-flight kv-cache preserved but SSE connection gets FIN from upstream. No 5xx from runtime.

2026-03-10 12:15 - Eng (Liam O'Connor): Hypothesis: LB connection-id rotation for long-lived SSEs triggers proxy path to tear down socket without proper SSE graceful drain, because keepalive/refcounting logic assumes requests are short-lived. Reproduced in staging by forcing conn-id rotation using lb-circuit tests.
2026-03-11 08:47 - Support (Maya Patel): Customer provided three sample X-Request-IDs and timestamps; attaching request ids for correlating logs: rq-17b4d2, rq-17b4d9, rq-17b540.

2026-03-11 11:30 - SRE (Anita Gomez): Confirmed correlation. Edge-proxy shows 'conn-rotate' marker then immediate FIN -> client disconnect. Worker reports continued token generation for ~100ms after FIN, then no final event emitted due to SSE stream closure upstream.

2026-03-12 09:05 - Eng (Liam O'Connor): Implemented temporary mitigation: edge-proxy patch holds rotated connections open for up to 5s to allow graceful SSE close events, and route sticky sessions for known-sse headers. Deployed to canary in us-east-1.
2026-03-12 12:40 - Customer (support@papertrail.example): Canary looks much better — on 25 long requests only 1 truncation observed. Will monitor for 24h and report back.

2026-03-12 17:20 - Support (Maya Patel): Marking ticket In Progress while we validate canary and schedule full rollback mitigation if stable. Follow-up items added to INT-4020 for long-term fix to connection lifecycle.
investigation_notes: SRE and Eng focused on edge-proxy/load-balancer interaction. Reproduced by artificially triggering conn-id rotation in staging. Key finding is that LB rotates logical connection identifiers for connection pool reconciliation; when rotation occurs mid-SSE, downstream edge-proxy does not propagate final SSE 'event: done' or trailing chunk to client before closing socket. Workers continue generation for a small window but there is no upstream to send final bytes to, resulting in truncated output.
findings: Root cause: conn-id rotation behavior in load-balancer control plane combined with edge-proxy's immediate socket termination semantics for recycled connections. Not a model or worker runtime crash. No quota limits hit. Occurs more frequently for long-lived SSEs (>30s) and under LB reconciliation events (scale-in/out or config reloads).
mitigation: Applied canary patch: edge-proxy now delays socket termination for rotated connections by configurable grace (default 5s) and honors SSE-specific drain header. Also enabled sticky route for requests with 'x-redwood-sse:1' to minimize rotation exposure. Canary deployed in us-east-1 dedicated pool.
next_steps: 1) Monitor canary metrics (truncation rate, conn rotate count) for 48h. 2) If stable, roll out patch cluster-wide and add e2e SSE tests that simulate LB rotations. 3) Create permanent change in LB controller to avoid rotating active SSE connections when possible. Tracked in INT-4020 and a follow-up PR to controller repo. 4) Update runbook to include detection of conn-id rotation correlating with SSE truncation.
resolution_notes: Temporary mitigation reduced truncation rate from ~35% to <5% in canary. Pending full rollout. Customer notified and monitoring window in progress. No data loss beyond truncation already observed; customers should implement client retry logic for partial responses as a short-term workaround.
timeline: 2026-03-10: Ticket opened and INC created. 2026-03-10 10:00: Initial SRE correlation to conn-id rotations. 2026-03-11: Reproduction in staging. 2026-03-12: Canary mitigation deployed. 2026-03-14: Planned full rollout decision date after 48h monitoring.
public_customer_message: We’re aware of truncated long-form chat responses in your dedicated pool. We’ve deployed a canary fix that significantly reduces occurrences and are monitoring. Recommended short-term client-side workaround: implement idempotent retries or request chunking for very long generations. We’ll follow up once the full rollout completes.
customer_confirmation: Customer confirmed reduced failure rate under canary and will validate for 24h. They requested a post-mortem and the timeline for a permanent fix.
